svg.title: Dodo Payments ledger-api DevSecOps architecture
svg.desc: End-to-end DevSecOps architecture: secure software supply chain, GitOps-managed zero-trust Kubernetes runtime, and authorized offensive validation, with findings mapped back to the controls that stop them.
svg.text: Ledger API: Secure Delivery, Zero-Trust Runtime & Offensive Validation
Dodo Payments DevSecOps assessment · local kind cluster · GitOps as the source of truth · PCI DSS scope
2 · GitOps-Managed Zero-Trust Kubernetes Runtime (Tasks 1 & 3) — kind cluster
ArgoCD reconciles Git desired state; Kyverno + Pod Security gate everything the API server accepts.
unsigned images from either ArgoCD or
payments namespace · NetworkPolicy: default-deny + explicit allow (L3/L4 layer)
Istio mesh · PeerAuthentication STRICT mTLS + AuthorizationPolicy default-deny (SPIFFE workload identity, not IP)
Underlying Kubernetes NetworkPolicy (default-deny + explicit allow by pod label) blocks at L3/L4 even for a workload
outside the mesh — defense-in-depth beneath Istio's L7 identity checks.
Outside attacker · black-box · no credentials · same brief that made Tasks 1–3 necessary in the first place.
TLS posture, and risk notes for a real attacker's view.
No exploitation, fuzzing, or scanners against any dodopayments host.
target: local-target lab (Docker) · production strictly out of scope
Findings: PAN disclosure (public app) · SSRF → internal-only service
↳ PAN fix: encrypted secrets, least-priv RBAC, read-only rootfs (Task 1)
↳ SSRF fix: default-deny NetworkPolicy + mTLS AuthorizationPolicy (Task 3)
Evidence to capture: Kyverno rejection · ArgoCD self-heal after a manual edit · istioctl authn tls-check (STRICT) · reporting→ledger-api 200 vs intruder→ledger-api blocked · Task 4 PoCs with CVSS.
